analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (the 'Last updated' date and one sentence about variable-frame-rate inline video) and docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (the date plus the GLM-5 native text request-control table). I found no executable code, wire-schema, key-handling, attestation, or authorization changes, so the T-053, T-054 and TB-011 boundaries are unchanged by this PR.

The documented GLM request-control changes describe provider behavior that I could not check, because no Swift source was supplied. They cover null/summary no-op reasoning members, the top-level `thinking` object, `json_object`/`json_schema` post-validation that withholds output until generation ends, and forced `tool_choice` via structured post-validation. The docs say failures are non-exposing (422 `tool_noncompliance` with no content) and that unsupported modes are rejected with 400. These claims appear consistent with the fail-closed posture in T-008 and with the treatment of provider output as untrusted in T-007. Unverified items:
- Whether GLM5NextPromptPolicy.swift, GLM5NextResponseFormat.swift and ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift actually implement the documented validation.
- Whether withheld JSON output can still leak partial content on failure.
- Whether the coordinator capability advertisement for forced tool_choice (tool-constraint protocol v1 for managed GLM identities) matches the platform.

The doc says the coordinator routes forced-tool requests to providers that advertise this capability. That routing is platform-owned and outside the supplied evidence.

The prefix-cache and passthrough-environment sections of cli-reference.md (T-041 context) were not modified; only unchanged context was visible. No finding qualifies. The changed 'Unqualified modes' text now drops the 'forced tool calls, strict tool decoding, JSON output modes' rejections, so those behaviors depend on the source changes in the same PR, which I did not see.
